terms.gloss: something heard with pleasure: a podcast
evidence: Nep. Att. 14.1: nēmō in convīviō ejus aliud acroāma audīvit quam anagnōstēn
Legio XIII and Quid Es Tu?, two Latin podcasts, of themselves
terms.comment: Classically “that which is heard with pleasure”, the music or reading that entertained guests at dinner, and also the performer who gave it (Lewis & Short); at Atticus’ table the only acroāma was a reader (Nep. Att. 14.1). Its use for a podcast is modern: it is the word Latin podcasters use for a podcast. The notes of Legio XIII speak of seriēs acroāmatum, and Quid Es Tu? opens its description dē acroāmate. Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini, and Andresian have no word for one.

phrases.latin: nēmō in convīviō ejus aliud acroāma audīvit quam anagnōstēn
phrases.english: at his dinners no one heard any entertainment but a reader
I listen to a podcast while I walk.

sources: Legio XIII (podcast), episode notes at podcasts.apple.com/podcast/id1338542908, read 16 November 2026.
Levi Baus, Quid Es Tu? (podcast), description at podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/quid-es-tu/id1508912347, read 16 November 2026.

acroama.html: The word is Greek ἀκρόαμα, as Lewis & Short itself gives it, and the Greek has a short first vowel. The Latin podcast Legio XIII writes it short too.
